title: The Wrong Zoom

beats.text: Imagine a stock jumping from three dollars to past twenty in a month.
Its company hasn't said a word since twenty fifteen.
March twenty twenty. Everyone's stuck at home on Zoom.
So you type ZOOM and hit buy.
So does everyone. The price needs a seatbelt.
Why is a silent company suddenly worth seven times as much?
The app is Z M. This ZOOM is a tiny firm last heard from in Beijing.
In twenty thirteen, a bankrupt chain called Tweeter jumped over tenfold when Twitter filed to go public.
You see, it's like grabbing a black suitcase off the airport belt because the tag looks right.
A Journal of Finance study found look-alike tickers move together.
On March twenty sixth, regulators froze ZOOM for ten trading days.
Everyone checked the ticker. Nobody checked the company.

facts.claim: Zoom Technologies (OTC ticker ZOOM) rose from around $3 a share in mid-February 2020 to more than $20 (high $20.90) about a month later, nearly sevenfold
Zoom Technologies had made no public disclosure since 2015
Its last reported principal executive offices were in Beijing, China
The SEC cited concerns about investors confusing it with a similarly named Nasdaq-listed issuer, Zoom Video Communications (ticker ZM)
The SEC suspended trading from 9:30 a.m. EDT March 26, 2020 through April 8, 2020 = ten business days (Section 12(k) limit)
In 2020 people worked from home and used the Zoom video app; ZM hit an all-time high March 19, 2020

Tweeter Home Entertainment, a consumer electronics retailer bankrupt since 2007, ticker TWTRQ, rose from about 1 cent to a 15-cent high on Oct 4, 2013 (over ten times) after Twitter filed IPO papers on Oct 3, 2013; FINRA halted it

Rashes, 'Massively Confused Investors Making Conspicuously Ignorant Choices (MCI-MCIC)', Journal of Finance 56(5), 2001: stocks with similar ticker symbols show significant comovement in returns, volume and volatility; deviations from fundamental value reverse within several days

caption:
March 2020: the world lived on one video app, so investors typed ZOOM and hit buy. Wrong company.
Zoom Technologies, silent since 2015, went from about $3 to over $20 in a month, until the SEC froze it.
